sentences.text: People are quietly replacing their phone keyboards with their voice.
Apps like Wispr Flow turn rambling speech into clean, ready-to-send text, in any app.
Here's who leads on iPhone, why people get hooked, and how a Swedish version could run entirely on the phone.
First, the plumbing: iOS won't let a keyboard use the microphone.
So every voice keyboard is two parts: a thin keyboard, and a main app that records in the background.
Starting a session means a trip to that app, and since iOS 26.4, users must swipe back by hand.
So who's winning?
Wispr Flow is the reference, with 4.8 stars from about seventeen thousand ratings.
9to5Mac called Aqua Voice the best dictation app its reviewer had ever used, and Make Tech Easier called Willow the most accurate.
Superwhisper, Typeless and Monologue round out the field, nearly all of them in the cloud.
The most interesting ideas come from the edges.
Aqua lets you edit by voice: make this shorter, translate it, spell a name.
Typeless keeps only what you meant when you change your mind mid-sentence.
And small apps like Outspoken and KeySay already run transcription and AI cleanup entirely on the phone.
Ranked by leverage, one feature dominates: text you don't have to edit.
Punctuation, filler words, self-corrections and lists, all handled.
Then come one-tap capture anywhere, getting names and jargon right, speed you can feel, and editing by voice.
Why do people get hooked?
Speaking is about three times faster than thumb-typing.
Wispr says eighty-nine percent of its messages go out without an edit, sent in about half a second.
People stop proofreading and start thinking out loud.
Wispr reports seventy percent of users still active after a year.
Trust turns into habit.
Can it all run locally? Yes, but not inside the keyboard.
iOS kills a keyboard at around seventy megabytes, so the models run in the main app.
There, the GPU is off limits, and from iOS 27 the Neural Engine needs a special entitlement.
On the CPU, Gemma 4 E2B writes about twenty-five tokens a second, so a full rewrite takes about four seconds.
Stream it into the text field instead, and words appear in about half a second.
And Swedish is wide open.
Apple's Swedish dictation adds no punctuation, and its new AI dictation in iOS 27 is English only.
Klang's Pianissimo model reaches about four and a half percent word error rate in Swedish, on the device.
Add cleanup that understands Swedish fillers, split compounds and number formats, and you have something nobody offers today.
The plan: nail edit-free Swedish text, make sessions painless, and learn each user's words.
Then add voice editing and translation.
Track one number above all: how often a message goes out untouched.
Talk, don't type. In Swedish. With nothing leaving the phone.
